body.statement: For constants \(0<c_{d,\alpha}\le C_{d,\alpha}<\infty\), \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2)\), and \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\). Consequently \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\).
body.justification: Uniform coverage and expected shortfall are treated as a decision problem distinct from point estimation.
body.gap: Ji--Lei--Spector prove broad dual-feasible uniform validity, and Manole--Balakrishnan--Wasserman prove near-minimax intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance; neither gives this all-arm one-sided endpoint-length converse.
body.consumer: A reported MOT tightening can be accompanied by a lower confidence endpoint whose worst-case conservatism is quantitatively controlled.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
\varepsilon_N=(\alpha N)^{-1/2}.
\]
Fix an arbitrary
\(\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_K)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\).
By Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array},
\(N=Km\), and hence, using the arm means in the frozen core,
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bar X
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m\mu_k
=\frac{m}{N}\sum_{k=1}^K\mu_k
=\bar\mu.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment} makes all centered summands
\(X_{ki}-\mu_k\) independent, so their cross inner products have mean
zero.  Since each \(P_k\) is a probability measure on \(\mathbb B_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2
=\mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}\|_2^2-\|\mu_k\|_2^2
\le 1.
\]
It follows from (1) that
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2
=\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
  \mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2
\le \frac{1}{N}.
\tag{2}
\]
The pointwise inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon_N\}
\le
\frac{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2}{\varepsilon_N^2}
\]
and (2) therefore give
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon_N\}
\ge 1-\alpha.
\tag{3}
\]
No asymptotic approximation is used in this step.

On the event in (3), the reverse triangle inequality yields
\[
\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-\varepsilon_N\}\le\|\bar\mu\|_2.
\]
Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives
\(L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2=V(\mathbf P)/K^2\ge0\).
Consequently Definition~\texttt{def:mean-lower-bound} implies
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}
=\bigl(\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-\varepsilon_N\}\bigr)^2
\le \|\bar\mu\|_2^2
\le L(\mathbf P)
\]
on an event of probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over
\(\mathbf P\).  Definition~\texttt{def:honest-bounds} thus proves
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha.
\tag{4}
\]

We next bound the expected excess length of this particular honest
rule.  Set \(q=\|\bar\mu\|_2\) and \(t=\|\bar X\|_2\).  Convexity of
\(\mathbb B_d\) gives \(q,t\in[0,1]\).  Theorem
\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives
\[
0\le L(\mathbf P)-q^2\le\frac r{K^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For every \(t\in[0,1]\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
0\le t^2-(t-\varepsilon)_+^2\le2\varepsilon.
\tag{6}
\]
Indeed, if \(t\ge\varepsilon\), the middle expression is
\(2t\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2\le2\varepsilon\); if
\(t<\varepsilon\), it is \(t^2\le t\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).
Also,
\[
|q^2-t^2|=(q+t)|q-t|
\le2\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2,
\tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality uses the reverse triangle inequality.
Combining (5)--(7) with
\((a+b)_+\le a+|b|\) for \(a\ge0\), and then applying the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and (2), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
 \bigl[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{mean}})_+\bigr]
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|q^2-t^2|
+\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\{t^2-(t-\varepsilon_N)_+^2\}\\
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+2\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2
+2\varepsilon_N\\
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+2N^{-1/2}
+2\alpha^{-1/2}N^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\mathbf P\) in (8), then using (4) as a
feasible rule in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length}, proves
\[
E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left(N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}\right)
\tag{9}
\]
for a finite positive constant \(C_{d,\alpha}\) depending only on
\(d\) and \(\alpha\).

For the matching all-procedure lower bound, invoke
Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}.  Write
\(L_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)})\), let
\(\Delta=L_1-L_0\ge aN^{-1/2}\), and denote the corresponding product
experiment laws by \(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1\).  They satisfy
\(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)\le1/4\).
For an arbitrary \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\), honesty at the lower
endpoint law and the defining total-variation inequality imply
\[
\mathbb Q_1(B_N\le L_0)
\ge\mathbb Q_0(B_N\le L_0)
  -\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)
\ge1-\alpha-\frac14
>\frac12,
\tag{10}
\]
where the last strict inequality uses \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\).  On
\(\{B_N\le L_0\}\), one has
\((L_1-B_N)_+\ge L_1-L_0=\Delta\).  Therefore
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bigl[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+\bigr]
\ge
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_1}[(L_1-B_N)_+]
\ge\frac{\Delta}{2}
\ge\frac a2N^{-1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Because (11) holds for every honest \(B_N\), taking the infimum in
Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length} proves the lower bound
with \(c_{d,\alpha}=a/2>0\).

Finally, if \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\), then \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\) and
\[
\frac r{K^2}\le\frac{d}{c_0^2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Equations (9), (11), and (12) yield
\(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:legal-triangular-array} restricts the admissible
asymptotic sequences through \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\); all inequalities
above are finite-sample statements at each admissible index, so this
restriction requires no further limiting step.
